report.verdict: A flattered beat: Q3-26 revenue +31% to €62.6m (~$68.9m) and Gaming Win +30% to €67.1m (~$73.8m) were helped by a World Cup July, a ~7pt peso tailwind (cc +23%) and a Mexico engine that is growing GW 39% but earning only €1.7m (~$1.9m) of Adj. EBITDA after the IEPS step-up. Guidance (€255-265m GW / €20-25m Adj. EBITDA) was reiterated rather than raised, Q4 was guided to single-digit growth against a €60.7m comp, and the regulatory calendar (Spain deposit limits, Colombia VAT) plus the parent's break-up sale process means the February 2027 outlook, not this print, decides the thesis.
summary: **Headline beat on growth, modest on profit:** Q3-26 revenue €62.6m (~$68.9m), +31% YoY; Gaming Win (GW) €67.1m (~$73.8m), +30% (+23% constant currency); Adj. EBITDA €4.2m (~$4.6m), +45% (6.7% of revenue, +60bps YoY but -230bps QoQ); IFRS net income €5.5m (~$6.1m) vs €1.4m. The only consensus marker available (Investing.com, ~€61.8m revenue) implies a ~1% revenue beat [consensus basis unverified].

**Mexico did the heavy lifting:** Mexico GW +39% to €37.2m (~$40.9m) (+26% cc), now 55% of group GW vs 52% a year ago; Spain +13% to €24.8m (~$27.3m); Other (Colombia/Panama/Buenos Aires) +86% to €5.2m (~$5.7m) on the lapping of Colombia's 2025 19% deposit VAT.

**Guidance reiterated, not raised — but 'upper part' flagged:** FY26 GW €255-265m (~$280-292m) and Adj. EBITDA €20-25m (~$22-27.5m), unchanged from the July upgrade (from €235-245m / €15-20m set in February). CFO now points to the upper part of the GW range. Implied Q4 GW €54-64m vs €60.7m (~$66.8m) in Q4-25, i.e. -11% to +5%; management explicitly guided Q4 to 'single-digit' growth. Implied Q4 Adj. EBITDA €3.9-8.9m vs €6.7m.

**Three named Q4 headwinds:** (i) no World Cup lift (July was 'exceptional'; Aug/Sep slowed, with the international break), (ii) the peso has 'given back most of this year's gains' against the euro since quarter-end, (iii) transition friction from Spain's new identification/deposit rules. CEO: 'we continue to be conservative.'

**World Cup quantified (from Q2 disclosure):** stakes €63m (~$69.3m), +180% vs WC2022; unique users +56% vs 2022 (ex-Colombia); ~40k new customers around the event; NGR >2x 2022 despite a low sports margin. All five Codere Online markets had teams; Spain won. Q3 captured the knockout stages/final (July).

**Growth is ARPU-led, not volume-led:** actives 166.8k, +5% YoY but -3.6% QoQ; spend per active €134/month (~$147), +24%. FTDs 91k (+7% on a tough comp) from ~251k registrations (36% conversion); CPA €209 (~$230) in-quarter, LTM ~€196 (~$216), described as stable. Casino 67% / sports 33% of GW. Note: Investing.com's '+50% actives' is an error — the company reports +5%.

**Cost base: taxes and marketing outgrew revenue, everything else lagged:** opex +29%; marketing €25.2m (~$27.7m), +37% (40.3% of revenue, +170bps YoY; 37.6% of GW); gaming taxes €13.6m (~$15.0m), +55% (21.7% of revenue, +330bps) on Mexico's IEPS rising from 30% to 50% from January 2026; platform & content +~10%; personnel +13%.

**Segment profitability diverges sharply:** Spain Adj. EBITDA €7.2m (~$7.9m), +24%, 29.0% margin (+~260bps); Mexico €1.7m (~$1.9m), -15%, 5.2% margin (-320bps) on tax and marketing timing; B2C Adj. EBITDA €9.6m (~$10.6m), +23% (9M €32.1m, +50%; LTM €43.6m, +59%); unallocated central costs ~-€5.4m (derived) vs ~-€4.9m. Spain is 75% of B2C EBITDA on 37% of GW.

**Earnings quality needs a second look:** IFRS EBITDA actually fell to €2.9m (~$3.2m) from €3.2m; the Adj. EBITDA bridge adds back €1.4m of LTIP expense in Q3 and €7.6m (~$8.4m) in 9M (≈47% of 9M Adj. EBITDA of €16.1m). Q3 net income includes a €3.4m (~$3.7m) non-cash gain on the warrant liability and €0.3m net interest income; ex-warrant NI ≈ €2.1m.

**Balance sheet is clean and cash converts:** total cash €65.6m (~$72.2m), of which €61.0m (~$67.1m) available (€4.6m reserved); no financial debt; NWC -€24.5m (~-$27.0m), structural; Q3 cash flow €3.0m (~$3.3m), 9M €16.4m (~$18.0m) ≈ 9M Adj. EBITDA €16.1m (~100% conversion). Cash up from €50.0m at Dec-25 and €62.6m at Jun-26. Warrant liability €2.1m; the 6.4m public warrants expire end-November 2026, removing P&L FV noise.

**Reporting change forced by the SEC:** following SEC staff review of the 2025 Form 20-F (now completed), 'Net Gaming Revenue' is renamed 'Gaming Win' and presented as a key operating metric rather than a revenue measure; historical amounts unchanged; guidance on the same basis. The SEC correspondence is to be made public — a governance item to read when it lands.

**NFL Mexico partnership:** multi-year Official Betting Partner of the NFL in Mexico (announced 10 Sep), including the NFL Mexico City Game on 22 Nov and Super Bowl LXI (Feb-27), with hospitality/VIP activations. Cost is inside guidance; CEO was candid that brand payback takes 'a couple of more seasons' — no near-term revenue effect modelled.

**Spain regulatory calendar is the 2027 swing factor:** nominative payment methods apply to new customers from end-October 2026 and to existing customers from April 2027; cross-operator joint deposit limits from March 2027 (Royal Decree 520/2026; defaults €700/day, €1,750/week, €3,300/4 weeks). CEO already sees an AML-driven slowdown in FTD acquisition; management frames limits as adjustable defaults and will 'educate' VIPs, and argues the rules favour scaled incumbents.

**Colombia VAT risk is back:** the 19% VAT on deposits that applied in 2025 could be reinstated in 2027, potentially for the full year (Bill 477 talks). CEO would revert to 'cash flow zero', keep the licence, cut investment and accept lower revenue; no exit. Other-segment GW (€15.3m 9M) is the exposure.

**Marketing stays heavy:** FY26 marketing to land in the 'high 90s, close to €100m' (~$110m) vs €86m (~$94.6m) in FY25 (of which €3-4m is peso translation); 2027 planned at a similar euro level with a lower % of GW. CEO: 'I'm fighting for marketing money.' This caps 2027 margin expansion to what GW growth delivers.

**Corporate overhang — parent break-up:** Codere Group (majority owner) hired Jefferies and Macquarie in March for a >€2bn (~$2.2bn) sale; with limited interest, Expansión (2 Nov) reports owners are exploring separate sales of the European, LatAm and listed online businesses. Grupo Codere Q3: gaming revenue +6% to €344m (~$378m), Adj. EBITDA +39% to €65.4m (~$72m). Change-of-control and minority-treatment risk is live.

**Optionality, not yet capital:** prediction markets (US Hispanic angle) 'nothing concrete'; Uruguay online regulation 'getting closer' (the same answer as a year ago); Brazil deliberately passed; board (Moshe Edree) stressed caution on new markets. Nothing here belongs in numbers yet.

**Thesis read-through:** the structural story (Spain operating leverage, 100% cash conversion, net cash) is intact, but Q3's +30% overstates the run-rate (cc +23%, World Cup, FX). Mexico's 50% tax means volume growth there is low-margin until marketing/GW falls; 2027 depends on Spain deposit limits and Colombia VAT. At ~$8.5/share the equity is ~€362m market cap / ~€296m EV (~$326m), ≈13x FY26E Adj. EBITDA midpoint and ~1.1x GW [estimates].

segments.name: Spain
segments.headline: The profit engine: +13% GW, Adj. EBITDA +24% to €7.2m at a 29% margin — but Q4/2027 carries the full weight of the new deposit and identification regime.
narrative: Spain revenue and Gaming Win, which are identical in this market (no IFRS accounting adjustments apply), rose 13% to €24.8m (~$27.3m), with average monthly actives up 5% to 52.8k and spend per active up 7% to roughly €157/month (~$172) on our derivation. Sequentially the picture is softer: GW fell 10% from the Q2 World Cup record of €27.6m (~$30.4m), actives slipped 3% and spend per active fell 7%, consistent with the CFO's description of an 'exceptional' July (Spain won the tournament) followed by an August/September lull and the international break. Over nine months Spain GW is up 18% to €77.9m (~$85.7m) with actives up 10% to 55.4k, so the first-half run-rate was materially stronger than Q3. Spain's share of group GW has slipped to 37% from 43% a year ago purely because Mexico outgrew it.

Profitability is where Spain earns its keep. Adj. EBITDA was €7.2m (~$7.9m), up 24%, implying a Q3-25 base of ~€5.8m and a margin of 29.0% versus ~26.4% a year ago (+~260bps). That is 75% of the company's B2C Adj. EBITDA of €9.6m (~$10.6m) generated on 37% of GW, and it is Spain that funds the marketing push in Mexico and the ~€5.4m of unallocated central costs. The company does not disclose Spanish market share, and we would not infer one; for context, the regulated Spanish online market generated GGR of €539m in Q2-26, +31% YoY (DGOJ data cited by CasinoBeats), which suggests Codere's +13% in Q3 (and +25% in Q2) is not obviously outgrowing the market. Market share: n/a.

The regulatory calendar is the issue the market will price. Nominative payment methods and new identification rules apply to new customers from the end of October 2026 and extend to existing customers in April 2027; cross-operator joint deposit limits take effect in March 2027 under Royal Decree 520/2026, with defaults of €700/day, €1,750/week and €3,300 per four weeks (per the Ministry release cited by CasinoBeats). The CEO already reports an AML-related slowdown in FTD acquisition that he expects the technology to resolve 'in the next few months', and both executives argued the limits are defaults customers can raise through the proper process, that players will either lift them or migrate between operators, and that VIP account managers will 'educate' the top tier. They also pitched the familiar line that such changes favour scaled incumbents. We are less sanguine: Spain's growth is ARPU-led (spend per active +7%) and the deposit-limit regime is aimed precisely at the high-value cohort; management itself cited 'transition effects' in Spain as one of three reasons Q4 growth slows to single digits.

No segment guidance is given, but the implied Q4 message is flat-to-low-single-digit growth in Spain against a Q4-25 comp we estimate at ~€24m (FY25 Spain-plus-Other NGR of €105.0m less 9M-25 €77.1m leaves ~€27.9m for the two combined). Looking into 2027 we would model Spain GW growth in the low single digits with the margin holding near 28-30%, and treat April 2027 (existing-customer nominative payments) as the quarter where friction peaks. Spain is also where the reporting relabel matters least: with no accounting adjustments, IFRS revenue and Gaming Win are the same number.

segments.name: Mexico
segments.headline: Volume and FX engine, not yet a profit engine: GW +39% (+26% cc) to €37.2m with spend per active +43%, but Adj. EBITDA fell 15% to €1.7m as the IEPS step-up to 50% and marketing absorbed the growth.
narrative: Mexico revenue rose 37% to €32.9m (~$36.2m) and Gaming Win 39% to €37.2m (~$40.9m); at constant currency GW grew 26%, so the stronger peso contributed roughly 13 points of the reported growth. It was the only segment to grow sequentially (GW +3% vs €36.1m in Q2), continuing an unbroken quarterly climb from €26.8m in Q3-25 through €32.8m, €34.6m, €36.1m and now €37.2m, with LTM GW of €140.6m (~$154.7m), +26%. The mix of growth is the notable thing: actives fell 3% YoY to 85.6k (and 3% QoQ), while spend per active rose 43% to ~€145/month (~$159), +6% QoQ. Management calls this a deliberate focus on 'customer quality'; a sceptic would call it rising VIP concentration in a market where the company runs on a white-label platform. The ~€4.3m gap between GW and IFRS revenue is the Mexico-specific accounting adjustment (revenue/GW ratio 88%, broadly stable).

Profitability went the other way. Mexico Adj. EBITDA was €1.7m (~$1.9m), down 15% from €2.0m, a 5.2% revenue margin (-320bps) or 4.6% of GW. The CFO attributed it to higher gaming taxes and higher marketing 'due to timing of certain provisions and expenses'. Group gaming taxes rose 55% to €13.6m (~$15.0m) — far ahead of revenue — mainly because Mexico's IEPS rate on gaming rose from 30% to 50% from 1 January 2026 under the 2026 fiscal package (per CasinoBeats; the CFO confirmed 'the tax increase in Mexico in place since January'). On a nine-month view the segment is still improving — Adj. EBITDA €8.2m (~$9.0m) vs €3.6m, LTM €12.2m (~$13.4m) vs €2.7m — but Mexico contributes just 18% of B2C Adj. EBITDA on 55% of GW. Until the marketing-to-GW ratio falls, each incremental peso of GW is taxed at 50% before marketing, which structurally limits drop-through.

Marketing is being spent for brand, not just CPA. The company became Official Betting Partner of the NFL in Mexico under a multi-year deal announced on 10 September that includes sponsorship of the NFL Mexico City Game on 22 November (49ers v Vikings) and Super Bowl LXI in February 2027, plus hospitality, VIP experiences, multi-city activations and merchandise rights. The spend is inside the current guidance; asked how it splits between Q4 and Q1-27, the CEO declined to quantify and was candid that sponsorship payback 'takes time, maybe this season, the next season'. Product cadence continues (a '99 Royale' launch with G Games in October). The presentation carries a market-sizing slide showing the Mexican online market at €2,457m in 2025A rising to €4,267m by 2028E and €5,667m by 2030E; against LTM GW of ~€141m that implies a mid-single-digit share [derived, and the slide's definition of market size is not stated — treat as indicative only].

The Q4 set-up is the inverse of Q3. The CFO said the peso 'has already given back most of this year's gains against the euro since the end of the quarter', the comp is a Q4-25 Mexico GW of €32.8m that itself grew 31%, and the CFO added that the company is 'a little bit more conservative... in terms of FX, in terms of margin, a little bit on sports' for Q4. Our arithmetic: constant-currency growth in the mid-to-high teens with a flat-to-negative FX contribution gives reported Mexico GW growth of roughly 4-8% in Q4 (~€34-35m), which is what underpins the group's 'single-digit' message. Beyond that, the questions for 2027 are whether actives can be re-grown without diluting ARPU, and whether the 50% IEPS rate is the final word from Mexico's fiscal authorities.

segments.name: Other (Colombia, Panama, City of Buenos Aires)
segments.headline: Rebound off a tax-depressed base: GW +86% to €5.2m as Colombia's 2025 deposit VAT lapsed and Panama kept compounding — but the VAT may be back for 2027.
narrative: The Other segment — Colombia, Panama and the City of Buenos Aires — reported revenue of €4.9m (~$5.4m) against €1.6m a year ago and Gaming Win of €5.2m (~$5.7m), up 86%, with actives up 37% to 28.4k and spend per active up 35% to ~€61/month (~$67). The comparison is flattered: in 2025 Colombian customers faced a 19% VAT on deposits (introduced by emergency decree and later removed), which crushed activity and left Q3-25 revenue at barely half of GW once levies were netted. With the tax gone earlier in 2026 the company re-invested and, in the CEO's words, 'bounced back quite nicely'. Sequentially the segment softened — GW -9% vs €5.7m in Q2, actives -7% — which is partly the World Cup roll-off. Nine-month GW is €15.3m (~$16.8m), +39%, on 28.4k actives (+26%).

Profitability is not disclosed for Other on its own; deducting Spain (€7.2m) and Mexico (€1.7m) from B2C Adj. EBITDA of €9.6m leaves roughly €0.7m (~$0.8m) versus about breakeven a year ago [derived, subject to rounding]. Panama was singled out as having performed 'very well' for several quarters after additional payment methods were added, in a stable regulatory and tax environment; the CEO's caveat is that the market is small with a cap on achievable share — 'I wish we had more Panamas'. Buenos Aires results carry IAS 29 hyperinflation adjustments that are stripped out of Adj. EBITDA. The presentation sizes these markets at €488m (Colombia), €29m (Panama) and €820m (Argentina) for 2025A, growing to €695m, €91m and €2,106m by 2030E [company slide, source not stated].

The risk is explicit: Colombia's government and Congress are in talks to reinstate the 19% VAT on online gambling deposits for 2027, potentially for the full year. The CEO called it 'very unfortunate' given the company had just scaled back up, and set out the playbook — revert to 'cash flow zero', maintain the licence, cut investment, lobby for mitigation, and accept 'some decrease in the revenues over there'. Exit is ruled out. Given Colombia is the bulk of a segment running at ~€20m of annualised GW, a full-year reinstatement would likely take the segment back toward its 2025 trajectory and remove a few million of GW from 2027; the EBITDA impact is small in absolute terms but the growth optics matter for a company guiding to double-digit GW growth.

On expansion, management was consistent and cautious. Uruguay remains 'getting closer' on the strength of Codere Group's retail presence and government dialogue, but the CEO conceded it is 'the same answer I could give you a year ago'. Board member Moshe Edree added that the company deliberately passed on Brazil and would want regulatory and country stability before entering markets such as Peru. Prediction markets (a Spanish-speaking US angle floated in media interviews) are being monitored, with 'nothing concrete' and no capital commitment discussed. None of this belongs in forecasts yet.

highlights.text: **Operating leverage is real below the marketing line:** platform & content +~10% and personnel +13% against revenue +31%; B2C Adj. EBITDA +23% to €9.6m (~$10.6m) in Q3, +50% to €32.1m (~$35.3m) in 9M; 9M group Adj. EBITDA more than doubled to €16.1m (~$17.7m) with period cash flow of €16.4m (~$18.0m) — ~100% cash conversion.
**Spain is a high-margin compounder:** Adj. EBITDA €7.2m (~$7.9m), +24%, 29.0% margin (+~260bps) on +13% GW; FTDs +7% group-wide on a World Cup-inflated comp with LTM CPA stable at ~€196 (~$216).

**Mexico scale keeps building:** GW +39% (+26% cc) to €37.2m (~$40.9m), six consecutive quarters of sequential growth, LTM Adj. EBITDA €12.2m (~$13.4m) vs €2.7m a year earlier even after the IEPS step-up to 50%.

**Fortress balance sheet for a ~€360m market cap:** €65.6m (~$72.2m) cash, no debt, NWC -€24.5m (~-$27.0m), cash up €15.6m since December; 6.4m public warrants expire end-November, removing the FV swing (€3.4m gain this quarter) from reported earnings.

**World Cup execution was strong and quantified:** stakes €63m (~$69.3m), +180% vs 2022; unique users +56%; ~40k new customers; NGR >2x 2022 — evidence the platform can monetise peak events across all five markets.
**Other markets re-accelerated:** GW +86% to €5.2m (~$5.7m) as Colombia normalised and Panama compounded; segment now roughly breakeven-to-positive at the Adj. EBITDA line [derived].

lowlights.text: **Headline growth overstates the run-rate:** +30% GW is +23% in constant currency, July was an 'exceptional' World Cup month, GW fell 3% QoQ, and Q4 is guided to single digits against a €60.7m (~$66.8m) comp — the implied Q4 range is €54-64m (-11% to +5%).

**Mexico earns almost nothing on 55% of GW:** Adj. EBITDA -15% to €1.7m (~$1.9m), 5.2% margin (-320bps) as gaming taxes rose 55% (IEPS 30%→50% from Jan-26) and marketing +37%; Mexico is 18% of B2C EBITDA. The tax rate is structural; the marketing 'timing' explanation is not yet evidenced.

**Adjusted vs IFRS gap is wide:** IFRS EBITDA fell to €2.9m (~$3.2m) from €3.2m; the LTIP add-back is €7.6m (~$8.4m) in 9M (~47% of Adj. EBITDA); Q3 net income of €5.5m includes a €3.4m non-cash warrant gain (ex-warrant ~€2.1m).

**Spain's regulatory wall is dated:** nominative payments for new customers now (CEO already sees an AML-driven FTD slowdown), existing customers April 2027, cross-operator deposit limits March 2027 — all landing on an ARPU-led Spanish business where spend per active, not actives, drives growth.
**Colombia VAT reinstatement risk for 2027:** management is already describing a 'cash flow zero' retreat; a full-year 19% deposit VAT would reverse most of the Other segment's 2026 rebound.

**Governance/corporate overhang:** the NGR→Gaming Win relabel was the outcome of an SEC staff review of the 2025 20-F (correspondence not yet public), and the majority owner is reportedly exploring a break-up sale that could include Codere Online on its own — change-of-control and minority-protection questions are now live.

**Marketing stays at ~€100m (~$110m), ~40% of revenue, into 2027:** CEO is 'fighting for marketing money'; absent a step-down in intensity, 2027 margin expansion is capped at what GW growth delivers, and that growth is guided to slow.

forecast.intro: The guidance bridge is one of reiteration, not revision. FY26 Gaming Win of €255-265m (~$280-292m) and Adj. EBITDA of €20-25m (~$22-27.5m) were first raised in July (from the February outlook of €235-245m NGR / €15-20m Adj. EBITDA) on the Q2 record and the World Cup; in November management held both ranges but nudged the GW message to the 'upper part'. With 9M GW of €201.0m (~$221.1m) and Adj. EBITDA of €16.1m (~$17.7m), Q4 is implied at €54-64m of GW versus €60.7m in Q4-25 and €3.9-8.9m of Adj. EBITDA versus €6.7m. The division driving the caution is Mexico (peso reversal since quarter-end on top of a 50% IEPS rate and a +31% Q4-25 comp), with Spain contributing regulatory 'transition effects'; Other is a 2027 rather than a Q4 issue. The moving parts for Q4 are the absence of July-style event uplift, a flat-to-negative FX contribution, NFL activation costs already inside the range, and marketing that the CFO expects to total 'high 90s, close to €100m' for the year (implying ~€24m in Q4).

forecast.view: Our own numbers [estimates]: **Q4-26E GW ~€63m (~$69m), +4% YoY** — Spain ~€24.5m (+~2%, friction from the October identification rules), Mexico ~€34m (+~4% reported, mid-teens cc, FX roughly neutral-to-negative), Other ~€4.8m; **Q4-26E revenue ~€59m and Adj. EBITDA ~€6m (~10% of revenue)**, with marketing ~€24m. That lands **FY26E at revenue ~€246m (~$271m), +~17%; GW ~€264m (~$290m), +~18%; Adj. EBITDA ~€22m (~$24m), ~8.4% of GW, +~60% vs €13.8m in FY25**, i.e. the GW upper half and the EBITDA midpoint. Year-end **net cash ~€70m (~$77m)** with no debt; leverage stays negative and we see no reason for the balance sheet to change absent M&A or a change of control. For 2027 (guidance due with FY results in late February) our base case is **GW growth of ~8-12%**: Mexico mid-teens cc less FX, Spain low single digits through the March/April deposit-limit and nominative-payment steps, and Colombia down if the 19% VAT returns for the full year. With marketing held at ~€100m, marketing/GW falls ~3pts and **Adj. EBITDA of ~€28-32m (~10-11% of GW)** is achievable — but the skew is to the downside because every identified 2027 variable (Spain limits, Colombia VAT, peso, Mexico fiscal appetite) is a headwind and the only tailwinds (NFL brand, prediction markets, Uruguay) are unquantified. On ~45m shares at ~$8.5 the equity is ~€362m market cap / ~€296m EV (~$326m): ~13x FY26E Adj. EBITDA midpoint and ~1.1x GW [estimates]. The swing factors are, in order, Spanish ARPU post-March 2027, the Colombian VAT decision, MXN/EUR, and whether the parent's process produces a standalone bid.
watch: Q4-26 GW print vs the €60.7m comp — does 'upper part' mean ≥€263m, and does Adj. EBITDA land above the €22.5m midpoint despite ~€24m of Q4 marketing?

Spain KPIs through Q1-Q2 2027: actives, spend per active and FTD run-rate as nominative payments extend to existing customers (April 2027) and cross-operator deposit limits start (March 2027, RD 520/2026 defaults €700/day, €1,750/week, €3,300/4 weeks).
Colombia: whether Bill 477 reinstates the 19% deposit VAT for 2027 and management's 'cash flow zero' response — size of the Other-segment reversal.
MXN/EUR: the peso 'gave back most of this year's gains' after quarter-end; Mexico is 55% of GW and ~€3-4m of FY26 marketing was pure translation.
Parent Codere Group's break-up sale process (Jefferies/Macquarie) — any standalone bid for Codere Online, treatment of minorities, and the related-party payables (~€7.4m to Codere Group).
February 2027 outlook: 2027 GW/EBITDA ranges, marketing envelope (~€100m flat?), CPA trend, and whether Mexico margin recovers once 'timing' items reverse.
FY26 Form 20-F and publication of the SEC comment correspondence behind the NGR→Gaming Win relabel; warrant expiry (30 Nov 2026) removing FV noise.
Optionality items with no numbers yet: prediction markets (US Hispanic), Uruguay regulation, NFL activation ROI over the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons.
